topic: What frequency planning challenges arise from co-locating 20/30 GHz beams in multi-satellite networks to avoid interference?
consensus_response: Co-locating 20/30 GHz beams in multi-satellite networks introduces significant frequency planning challenges due to large antenna sidelobes, causing intra-system interference and reducing spectral efficiency by up to 25%. The spatial correlation properties of the channel affect the effectiveness of precoding in mitigating inter-beam interference. Precoding can mitigate inter-beam interference but its effectiveness depends on spatial correlation properties. Advanced techniques such as multi-user precoding or machine learning-based interference cancellation can be employed to adaptively mitigate inter-beam interference.
reference_context: The reference context provides various studies and data on the challenges of co-locating 20/30 GHz beams, including reduced spectral efficiency due to intra-system interference, and the importance of advanced techniques such as precoding and machine learning-based interference cancellation to mitigate inter-beam interference.
